reading.body:
Carrie Adams is named on three Lobbying Disclosure Act filings about AI, all filed through one lobbying firm for a single client, THE AI POLICY NETWORK INC.

The record is narrow and consistent. One lobbyist, one firm, one client, three AI filings. The fourteen bills listed are the legislative targets those filings name, not separate engagements, and the page does not say which bill appears on which filing or how the three filings divide across them. What the disclosures do establish is the prior government service: Communications Director and Senior Advisor to Senator Fetterman, Deputy Digital Director and Digital Director for Senator Schumer, Digital Director for Speaker Pelosi, Senior Advisor to the House Committee on Rules, Senior Advisor to Representative Louise Slaughter, and Communications Director for Representative B. Lee. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, so this is a statutory disclosure rather than an inference.

For AI specifically, the pattern is the one that matters across the sector. AI policy is being shaped through the same staffing pipeline that runs the rest of Washington, and the people who wrote or coordinated digital and communications strategy for senior legislators now represent an AI policy client before those same institutions. Compute, buildings, and power set the physical ceiling on AI scaling, but the rules that determine where data centers get built, how they get powered, and what models are permitted are written by people, and this record shows one of the people in that loop.

What the data does not cover is large. It gives no dollar amounts, no lobbying expenditures, no dates of contact, no text of any filing, and no outcome. It does not say what position the client took on any of the fourteen bills, whether any bill passed, or whether the lobbying had any effect. It also does not establish that the prior positions and the current AI work are connected beyond the fact that the same person holds both. The page states what the filings disclose and draws no conclusion about the person, and neither should a reader.
